<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
T09 requires careful review. Much of the Bean Validation is already partially in place from earlier tasks.

T09 requires API-boundary validation for create, patch, comment, and transition requests. PatchTicketRequest needs `@NotBlank` on title and description when present, replacing service-level checks with conditional Bean Validation. Empty PATCH bodies and client-supplied status must be rejected. Verification tests will check blank titles, oversized bodies, and unknown priority strings.

CreateTicketRequest currently rejects client-supplied status in the service layer. T09 requires moving that check to the API boundary. Empty PATCH bodies are already rejected in the service and could be promoted to a class-level constraint. Unknown priority strings cause Jackson to throw HttpMessageNotReadableException, which returns a generic Spring error instead of VALIDATION_ERROR. T10 is meant to map this properly.

Jackson may need explicit configuration to reject unknown properties and enforce proper enum deserialization. ApiExceptionHandler currently only catches InvalidTransitionException, so it likely needs minimal MethodArgumentNotValidException handling to support T09 verification. The plan defers full error mapping to T10.

T09 only needs to reject invalid inputs with 400s. Full contract-compliant error bodies are deferred to T10. Spring Boot's default `@Valid` failure format may not match the required contract, so T09 must ensure validation produces proper 400 responses.

The current PatchTicketRequest uses `@Size` on getters, which passes empty strings because size zero satisfies the constraint. Blank title or description values therefore bypass validation and must be caught by service logic. A class-level `@AssertTrue` validator is being considered to enforce presence-aware validation across the request.

The chosen approach for PatchTicketRequest is method-level `@AssertTrue` validators. One will enforce `title` is not blank when present. Another will reject empty PATCH bodies. This keeps validation at the API boundary without relying on service-layer checks.

A cleaner approach for CreateTicketRequest is to annotate the `status` field directly with `@Null`. This rejects client-supplied status at the API boundary without extra method-level validators. Empty PATCH bodies are already handled by the service layer. TransitionTicketRequest already enforces `@NotNull` on its fields.

Blank status values will fail Jackson enum deserialization automatically. Unknown priority strings are already rejected by Spring Boot's default behavior. For PatchTicketRequest, direct `@NotBlank` on title or description would fail on omitted fields, so method-level `@AssertTrue` validators are needed instead. The implementation will begin with adding `@Null` to CreateTicketRequest.status.

PatchTicketRequest will gain class-level `@AssertTrue` validators rejecting empty bodies, blank titles or descriptions when present, and any client-supplied status. Existing `@Size` annotations remain. Minimal exception handler changes are unnecessary; T09 only needs to enforce validation at the API boundary.

Blank assignee strings are valid per the data contract and must not trigger validation errors. I am also reviewing the data model for additional field limits and checking for existing Jackson configuration.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Starting implementation of T09. Reviewing the incomplete requirements to identify gaps before coding.

Mapping out the Bean Validation changes for T09. CreateTicketRequest needs `@Null` on status. PatchTicketRequest needs `@AssertTrue` for empty bodies, forbidden status updates, and non-blank title or description fields. TransitionTicketRequest and AddCommentRequest already have adequate annotations. The service layer will drop redundant checks now handled by the API boundary.

Realized that missing exception handlers would return default Spring errors instead of the required VALIDATION_ERROR contract shape. Adding minimal handling for MethodArgumentNotValidException and HttpMessageNotReadableException in ApiExceptionHandler. This risks overlapping with T10, which also covers stable error JSON and contract code mapping.

Partial validation error mapping in T09 is justified because hard rules require meaningful responses. ApiExceptionHandler will map MethodArgumentNotValidException, ConstraintViolationException, and HttpMessageNotReadableException to VALIDATION_ERROR. This keeps T10 thinner.

Re-reading T09 confirmed it only requires rejecting invalid requests, not mapping every exception to T10 contract codes. The scope narrows to Bean Validation annotations and API-boundary rejection alone. PatchTicketRequest will use public boolean `isXxx` or `getXxx` methods for `@AssertTrue` constraints. The controller already carries `@Valid`.

Confirmed that `@Null` on status rejects explicit values while allowing omitted fields. Redundant service-layer status checks will be removed, leaving normalization and trimming intact. Custom messages for the `@AssertTrue` constraints are being drafted.

Drafted the exact `@AssertTrue` constraint methods for PatchTicketRequest. `isPatchNonEmpty()` requires at least one updatable field. `isStatusAbsent()` blocks status updates via PATCH. `isTitleValidWhenPresent()` enforces non-blank titles when present.

Confirmed the validation order works correctly. A request containing only status triggers both the empty-body and status-absent failures, so the status-rejection rule takes precedence. An empty body also fails the non-empty check. The contract accepts returning two distinct validation errors when both constraints apply. Size violations on the title getter and blank-title failures through AssertTrue are handled separately.

Confirmed that null title or priority values trigger AssertTrue failures. Unknown priority strings cause Jackson deserialization errors before validation runs, so the default 400 response suffices. No WebMvcTest is required for this task; manual curl verification will suffice. T09 will be marked complete in plan.md.

Adding `@NotBlank` with clear messages for create and patch requests. Assignee fields allow blank values and normalize to null in the service. Whitespace-only titles are rejected by `@NotBlank` and trimmed. A thin validation exception handler is still needed to prevent Spring Boot 4 from returning generic Problem Details.

Decided against adding validation exception handling in T09. The ApiExceptionHandler comment explicitly defers broader 4xx/5xx mapping to T10, so T09 stays limited to Bean Validation annotations and API-boundary rejection. `@Validated` is unnecessary alongside `@RequestBody @Valid`. Ready to implement the annotations and simplify the service, then verify rejections with curl.
</details></think>

PatchTicketRequest validation has a subtle flaw. A request containing only a status field fails both `isPatchNonEmpty` and `isStatusAbsent`.

The validation logic is sound. Status-only requests correctly trigger status rejection. Empty bodies correctly trigger empty rejection. Both fields together pass validation. The API contract treats both errors as 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. This is acceptable.

Empty PATCH bodies correctly fail validation. Status fields on creation are properly rejected. Unknown priority values may cause Jackson failures. Hibernate validates all constraints by default. Title-only updates pass cleanly. Next step is to build, test, and mark T09 complete in plan.md.

A dedicated validation exception handler was considered for T09 to satisfy the meaningful error requirement. That work is deferred to T10 instead.

Explicit null status fields on creation currently pass validation because `@Null` accepts null. The API contract requires rejecting any present status field, so null status must also be rejected during ticket creation.

CreateTicketRequest is a record, so it cannot easily distinguish a null status from a missing field. Converting it to a class with explicit presence tracking will allow rejecting null status values while still accepting absent keys.

The chosen implementation for CreateTicketRequest is a class with a boolean flag tracking whether the status field was actually present in the JSON. A custom setter on the status property will set this flag to true whenever a value is provided. This mirrors the PatchTicketRequest pattern exactly and allows the validator to reject explicit null status values while still permitting absent keys.
</details></think>
